### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Frontiers 'collaborative peer review': single-anonymized (reviewers know author identity), platform-mediated direct dialog between authors, reviewers and handling editor; names of editors and all endorsing reviewers are published with the article. ### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is a publisher-wide (Frontiers-group) policy, not journal-specific — no Frontiers in Public Health–specific AI policy page was found, separate from the general Frontiers editorial policy. Facts (per 2026-07 fetch of the Frontiers policies page): generative AI may be used for text/figure generation and editing, but must be disclosed in the acknowledgments (name, version, model, source of the tool); AI cannot be listed as author/co-author; authors remain responsible for factual accuracy/citations of AI-assisted content; uploading of prompts/outputs as supplementary files is encouraged but not mandatory; editors/reviewers are barred from uploading unpublished manuscript content into external AI tools during review (confidentiality). Frontiers also announced (April 2026, per frontiersin.org/news and EurekAlert press release) a broader 'AI practical guidance' framework covering the whole publication lifecycle, moving from binary allow/ban toward disclosed, responsible-use routes — directional/leniency-raising but not journal-section-specific in the sources found. Leniency scored 3/5: disclosure-gated use is allowed (not banned), but unverified/undisclosed AI content and AI-authorship are prohibited; independent commentary (pivot-to-ai.com, 2026-07-02) frames the newer policy as effectively pushing editors toward AI-tool use — an adversarial framing not corroborated first-hand here. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/policies-and-publication-ethics |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes — Frontiers states a 'supportive preprint policy': authors may post to preprint servers before/during review, provided the server does not restrict the author's full copyright/re-use rights; preprints should be cited in the manuscript.
> Source: https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/policies-and-publication-ethics

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

A zhihu article ("Frontiers in Public Health：'灌水神刊'，审稿超快的公共卫生SCI", zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1944419450876069010) explicitly frames the journal with the pejorative Chinese label '灌水神刊' (roughly 'mass dump-publishing journal') and touts fast review as a selling point for volume publication — this is a reputational/marketing claim from a paper-mill-adjacent SEO-style site, not a first-hand reviewer account (the article itself returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so this is search-snippet text only — low confidence).
